Story's Credibility ![Original Reporting](https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/img-oi03r0q.png?auto=format%2Ccompress&w=32) ## Who I am, and why these three words keep coming up I've been writing software for more than 25 years, mostly in education technology, behavioral analytics and data science. I recently started my tenth company as technical founder. I'm also co-founder and chairman of Saigon A.I., a doctoral researcher at the University of St Andrews working between educational psychology and artificial intelligence with a focus on self-regulated learning (SRL), and the builder of QCoda, an AI governance platform focused on governing AI-assisted software engineering. QCoda started with a pattern I kept running into, in my own teams and in teams I advised. We'd make a dozen consequential decisions while planning an AI feature. Which model. Which data. Where it runs. Who gets to see the prompts. Nobody wrote any of it down. Months later an auditor (or a customer's security team, or a regulator) would ask why we did it that way, and the honest answer was that nobody really decided. It just happened. Governance showed up after the mistake, as punishment. That's the lens I bring here. Almost every AI architecture conversation I have now includes one of three words: *sovereign*, *decentralized* or *private perimeter*. People use them interchangeably. They shouldn't. Each one answers a different question and protects a different party, and none of them answers the question that actually gets teams in trouble. highlights.content: ### TCI Media: Home of the Wire Publications ![Header Logo 1](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/ai-600-300x73-1.webp) ![Header Logo 2](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/bigdatawire-logo.webp) ![Header Logo 3](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/qc-600-300x69-1.webp) ![Logo](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/hpc-logo-300x60-1.jpg) ## Off the Wire Press Releases ### October 12, 2026 ### October 9, 2026 ### October 8, 2026 ### October 7, 2026 ## H2O-Lightning-4B Ranks 1st on JevBench Open-Weights Leaderboard *A 4-billion-parameter open-source decision model finishes ahead of 103 open-weight systems, including some built on base models nearly eight times its size, on a benchmark that weighs intelligence, calibration, speed and cost equally.* MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif., Oct. 12, 2026 — [H2O.ai](https://h2o.ai/), the trusted Sovereign AI Platform for predictive, generative and agentic AI, with observability built in, today announced that **H2O-Lightning-4B**, its open-weights decision model, ranked first among 104 open-weight systems on the [JevBench Composite Score leaderboard](https://h2o.ai/blog/2026/h2o-lightning-jevbench/) as of Oct. 7. The model scores 72.5 out of 100, above the 71.5 posted by Jev, the benchmark’s closed API reference system, at an estimated $0.021 per 1,000 decisions. [![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px-300x300.jpg)](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px.jpg)Much of the AI work inside banks, insurers, health systems, telcos and government agencies is a decision about a record: route this ticket, flag this clause, score this claim. TypeSafe AI built Jev around that idea. Jev is a model that answers a typed question with a calibrated probability instead of generated text. Each decision needs the right answer, a probability a risk team can set a threshold on, a latency that fits a live workflow, and a cost that stays predictable at millions of calls a month. JevBench scores all four on an equal-weight harmonic mean, so a weak axis drags down the whole score. An open 4-billion-parameter model scoring above a closed reference system is the shift regulated buyers have been waiting for. Owning the model no longer means giving up quality. ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px-300x300.jpg) “Better decisions don’t need bigger models. Classification is one of the most common enterprise use cases, and models like H2O-Lightning deliver frontier-model quality and lightning-fast decisions at about 100 times lower cost. Leading AI companies, including Microsoft, are now building decision models of their own. This is not a flash in the pan,” said Sri Ambati, Founder and CEO of H2O.ai. **How It Works** H2O-Lightning-4B is a fine-tune of Qwen3.5-4B. It answers typed decision questions about a record such as a document, ticket, policy or conversation, and returns a probability for every option. It supports three question types: choice (one of a set of named options), yes/no (the probability that a statement is true) and score (an ordinal level on a stated scale, with its probability distribution). Each decision is one forward pass and one output token, so cost is driven by input tokens alone. The model runs on unmodified vLLM 0.30.0 with a small standard-library shim in front. **The Results** H2O-Lightning-4B competes in a crowded, fast-moving field. TypeSafe AI set the bar with Jev. Independent developers and enterprise teams have since put more than 100 open-weight systems on the JevBench board, and its maintainers score every entry the same way. highlights.content: **[Help Net Security newsletters](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/newsletter/)**: Daily and weekly news, cybersecurity jobs, open source projects, breaking news – **[subscribe here!](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/newsletter/)** Please turn on your JavaScript for this page to function normally. ![Anamarija Pogorelec](https://img.helpnetsecurity.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/16092207/anamarija_pogorelec-100x100.jpg) [Anamarija Pogorelec](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/author/anamarijapogorelec/ "Author archive: https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/author/anamarijapogorelec/"), Senior Staff Writer, Help Net Security **Share** # Microsoft’s new model helps AI agents judge their next move Microsoft-Decision-1 is a small decision-scoring model. Given a situation, a question and a fixed set of [answer options](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/03/sans-aws-agentic-ai-security/), it returns a calibrated probability for each option. “This model is designed for routing, classification, prioritization, verification, and workflow control, making it easier to incorporate decision intelligence into existing applications, agents, and workflows in a secure, trusted environment,” [Achint Srivastava](https://www.linkedin.com/in/achint/), VP of Software Engineering in Microsoft’s Office of the CTO, [explained](https://commandline.microsoft.com/microsoft-decision-1-model-foundry/). ### How Microsoft-Decision-1 works Microsoft said it evaluated the model across 36 benchmarks covering nearly 150,000 questions, with the benchmarks kept blind from training. In the company’s benchmarking, Microsoft-Decision-1 was 2.5 times faster than H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1, the runner-up on speed, and about 35 times faster than [GPT-6 Sol](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/23/gpt-6-sol-luna-lower-api-prices/) in median latency. Accuracy, latency and calibration, side by side (Source: Microsoft) The probability scores indicate the model’s confidence in each answer and can help an application decide whether to act, defer a decision or request a review. Microsoft advises developers to validate the model and confidence thresholds on examples representative of their intended use. Microsoft-Decision-1 was post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B for single-pass scoring. The company plans to base future versions on other models, including those from [Microsoft AI](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/15/microsoft-ai-safety-rules-humanist-ai-code-of-conduct/) and OpenAI. The model supports yes/no questions, multiple-choice questions, rating scales and rubric-based grading of AI responses and agent actions through structured API calls. It is not designed for open-ended text generation, conversation, translation or summarization. The company identified speed, performance across tasks, robustness, probability calibration and safety as challenges in developing the model. ### Internal testing Microsoft is testing Microsoft-Decision-1 on tasks including sorting customer feedback, evaluating AI answers and finding relevant information during service incidents. Xbox researchers used it to group more than 10,000 pieces of feedback and reviews from surveys, STEAM and X into predefined categories. Microsoft said the results were competitive in quality with GPT-6 Sol’s, with processing more than 14 times faster at one two-hundredth of the cost. The Copilot team tested the model’s ability to assess chat and agent responses. Microsoft reported results competitive with [GPT5.6 Luna’s](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/29/openai-gpt-5-6-models-preview/), with processing 100 times faster. In incident-response tests, Microsoft-Decision-1 performed better and faster at retrieving relevant information than the large language model used for comparison. Microsoft also tested the model in Microsoft Discovery, where [AI agents](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/25/ariel-assaraf-coralogix-ai-agent-guardrails/) evaluate experiment results and revise their next steps. On the long-horizon coding benchmark SWE-Marathon, both new models surpass Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. Trained at the gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center, the models support 1 million-token context windows and native multimodal input, with core capabilities including Active Memory and Active Focus. The standard version is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens via API; the Full variant is available exclusively through Muse Code subscriptions at $50 or $200 per month. The launch marks Meta's formal entry into the top tier of global AI model competition. ##### Key Elements ![Meta Unveils Flagship Muse Wonder Models, Closing In on Global AI Intelligence Lead](https://img.biggo.com/zO7vZ-lOHGJ2KD6iQCb9n5vlvQNyyvFR_oeefZ19nEg/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTEwLzgzOTdhMWE5LWEzOGItNDM0Zi1hMzRiLTE1ZWIzOWNhMDQxNV8xNzkxODU0MDEyX2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Meta's competitive posture in artificial intelligence has undergone a fundamental shift. On October 12 local time, the social media giant unveiled two next-generation large models in a single release—Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full. The company describes the pair as its most powerful model lineup to date, calling the launch a historic leap toward "personal superintelligence." On third-party evaluator Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, Muse Wonder Full scored 56 points, tying Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5 for the top tier globally and directly edging out OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra. The standard Muse Wonder scored 52 points, comprehensively surpassing its predecessor, Muse Spark 1.3. This means Meta—long cast as a catch-up player in the AI model race—has for the first time positioned itself on equal footing with OpenAI and Anthropic on core intelligence metrics. ### Benchmarks Place Meta in the Top Tier According to Artificial Analysis, only six weeks separated the release of Muse Spark 1.3 from the new models, yet the Intelligence Index jumped from 48 to 56 points—an 8-point surge. Across all ten tests, the new models outperformed their predecessor; six results landed in the top three, with two taking first place. In GDPval-AA v2.1, which assesses professional knowledge work, Full ranked second with an Elo rating of 1857. It also placed third in three additional categories: knowledge work AA-Briefcase, business process automation AutomationBench-AA, and scientific programming SciCode. Terminal operation capability is a standout upgrade. Terminal-Bench 4.0 requires AI to autonomously read files, execute commands, and troubleshoot errors. highlights.content: Updated : Tuesday, October 13, 2026, 10:29 * [Home](/) * [Login](https://www.businesskorea.co.kr/member/login.html) * [Sign in](https://www.businesskorea.co.kr/member/index.html) * [Korean](/?editcode=MAIN_13) [![Businesskorea](/image/logo/toplogo_20230426040837.png) ![](/image/logo/year_40.png)](/) [![Businesskorea](/image/logo/printlogo_20230426040837.png)](https://www.businesskorea.co.kr) MangoBoost Teams Up With AMD to Challenge Nvidia in AI Inference Scroll Move Status-bar # MangoBoost Teams Up With AMD to Challenge Nvidia in AI Inference * *Editor* Park Jung-hwan * 2026.10.13 09:48 ## Korean Startup Unveils Serverless AI Platform, Targets 500MW Infrastructure Expansion ![AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su speaks at an AI semiconductor industry roundtable held at the Four Seasons Hotel in Jongno-gu, Seoul, on Oct. 7, 2026.](/news/photo/202610/278642_286325_475.jpg) AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su speaks at an AI semiconductor industry roundtable held at the Four Seasons Hotel in Jongno-gu, Seoul, on Oct. 7, 2026. South Korean AI infrastructure startup MangoBoost is expanding its collaboration with Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) as it seeks to challenge Nvidia’s dominance in the artificial intelligence market through an integrated approach to hardware, software and AI inference services. AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su has highlighted the startup as an example of AI infrastructure development in South Korea, underscoring the growing relationship between the two companies. Kim Jang-woo, CEO of MangoBoost and a professor at Seoul National University, unveiled the company's new AI inference platform, Mango Inference, during a press conference at the Grand InterContinental Seoul Parnas in Gangnam, Seoul, on Oct. 12. “MangoBoost is no longer simply a component company,” Kim said, announcing the company's transformation into an AI factory operator that designs and integrates hardware and software to deliver AI services directly to customers. Mango Inference is a serverless inference service that enables businesses and developers to access AI models using a single API key without building their own server infrastructure. Users can select open-weight models, including DeepSeek and GLM, and pay according to usage. The company said its proprietary inference optimization software, LLMBooost, reduces bottlenecks in data transfers between storage devices and GPUs, lowering costs by at least 20% compared with existing high-performance services. A central element of MangoBoost's expansion strategy is its close collaboration with AMD, which is competing with Nvidia in the AI GPU market. While AMD has been working to strengthen its networking and software ecosystem, MangoBoost contributes system-level design and optimization capabilities. The companies' joint technical achievements have also been featured on AMD's official blog. During her visit to South Korea on Oct. 7, Su cited MangoBoost as a notable example of domestic AI infrastructure development and maintained close communication with Kim, according to the company. Kim said the relationship has also strengthened MangoBoost's ability to secure GPU supplies. He explained that the company has established a roadmap for obtaining a stable supply of AMD's latest GPUs and has drawn up plans to procure tens of thousands of units. To improve service reliability and operational efficiency, MangoBoost is building a 1-megawatt (MW) AI infrastructure facility near Dosan Park in Seoul's Gangnam district. The facility is already partially operational, with AMD's latest Instinct-series GPUs being introduced in phases. Full completion is targeted for the first quarter of 2027. By increasing the proportion of internally designed systems, MangoBoost aims to reduce its reliance on external cloud providers and improve overall operating efficiency. Logo, Blocks&Files](/view-resources/dachser2/public/blocksandfiles/logo-white.svg)](https://www.blocksandfiles.com) BANDF AD # Uvi gives AI agents enterprise context Chris Mellor [Chris Mellor](https://www.blocksandfiles.com/author/chris-mellor) STORAGE EDITOR Blocks & Files editor Published Israeli startup [Uvi](https://www.uvi.io/) says enterprises enterprises are paying frontier AI companies to repeatedly re-learn what their own businesses already know but cannot surface. It can reveal this hidden context using knowledge graph technology. Uvi says every AI agent an enterprise deploys starts work knowing nothing about the company it works for. It has to reconstruct that context from scratch, and the company pays a frontier model every time it does. It has knowledge graph technology to give Claude, Gemini, GPT and every other AI tool a company uses the missing context behind its decisions, conversations and code, creating a context reasoning layer the company owns once and can make available to every agent it runs. ![Gilad Salinger.](https://image.blocksandfiles.com/5302518.webp?imageId=5302518&x=0.00&y=0.00&cropw=100.00&croph=100.00&width=960&height=960&format=jpg) Gilad Salinger CEO and co-founder Gilad Salinger said: "Enterprise context is a problem that gets bigger as AI adoption grows. Early use cases exposed accuracy gaps. Today, the conversation has shifted to cost and tokens. But as companies move into more complex agentic workloads, the real bottleneck becomes speed. And speed depends on context: understanding what the organization knows, what other agents are changing in parallel, and the history behind those decisions, then narrowing it down to exactly what each agent needs to keep moving." BANDF AD Keeping a semantic layer, a knowledge graph and the reasoning layer on top relevant, permissioned and in sync with live data is the heavy lifting no engineering team wants to own. Uvi says it does it for them. ![Dror Wolmer.](https://image.blocksandfiles.com/5302523.webp?imageId=5302523&x=0.00&y=0.00&cropw=100.00&croph=100.00&width=960&height=960&format=jpg) Dror Wolmer Salinger and CTO Dror Wolmer, both in Tel-Aviv, founded Uvi in 2023 to build the substrate enterprise AI agents need to act inside organizations, not just summarize documents. It was initially called Naboo. Salinger is an ex-VP technology at Nutrifresh Services, which acquired Fetchy, a company he founded, while Wolmer is an ex-security researcher and CTO of Cognigo, which was acquired by NetApp. Naboo said it was building a “Reasoning Layer” (also called an enterprise context or semantic layer) for AI agents so they can act inside organizations rather than just summarize documents. Enterprise AI agents often fail or become expensive because organizational knowledge is scattered across systems (code, tickets, PRs, Slack, docs, monitoring) and the why behind decisions is rarely explicitly recorded. Naboo/Uvi addresses this by constructing a Decision Graph. highlights.content: SecurityBrief Asia - Technology news for CISOs & cybersecurity decision-makers [![SecurityBrief Asia logo](/brands/sb-new-logo.svg)](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.asia) ![Acalvio launches ShadowPlex AI Agent in Gemini marketplace](https://securitybrief.asia/uploads/story/2026/10/13/Ram_Varadarajan-story-321217.webp) [Cloud Security](https://securitybrief.asia/tag/cloud-security) [Cybersecurity](https://securitybrief.asia/tag/cybersecurity) [Agentic AI](https://securitybrief.asia/tag/ai-agents) # Acalvio launches ShadowPlex AI Agent in Gemini marketplace Tue, 13th Oct 2026 (Today) [![Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://securitybrief.asia/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor](/author/joseph-gabriel-lagonsin) Acalvio has launched its ShadowPlex AI Agent in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Marketplace, linking its deception security software with Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise. The launch gives security teams a new way to create deception playbooks by describing a security objective in natural language. The agent then generates a strategy, deployment plan and playbook for use through Acalvio's ShadowPlex platform. Deception tools are used to mislead attackers, detect reconnaissance and expose unauthorised movement through systems. Acalvio is introducing the agent as companies face a rise in AI-assisted attacks, including faster reconnaissance, credential abuse and lateral movement across networks. The agent is intended to reduce the specialist knowledge usually needed to build and deploy deception programmes. Tasks that often required experienced deception engineers can now be completed in minutes through an AI-driven workflow. **How it works** Security teams can enter objectives such as detecting lateral movement, identifying credential abuse, protecting privileged identities or securing enterprise AI agents and AI-enabled infrastructure. The agent then reasons through the requirement and returns a structured deception playbook ready for deployment. The system is designed for both conventional enterprise environments and newer AI-focused deployments. Playbooks can be created for on-premises infrastructure, cloud environments, identity systems, IT and OT networks, and enterprise AI infrastructure. That broad scope reflects two security pressures facing many large organisations. One is attackers' use of AI to automate and accelerate intrusion activity. The other is the rapid adoption of AI agents and AI-enabled workflows inside companies, creating a new set of systems and identities that also need protection. **AI Focus** The ShadowPlex AI Agent is designed to address both sides of that trend. In one use case, security teams can generate playbooks to disrupt AI-driven reconnaissance, credential abuse and lateral movement. In another, they can use the same approach to protect internal AI agents, workflows and infrastructure from misuse, compromise and unauthorised access. For cybersecurity vendors, the ability to tie products to large AI ecosystems has become increasingly important as customers look for tools that fit into existing cloud and AI software estates. Placement in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Marketplace gives Acalvio visibility within Google Cloud's enterprise AI environment and could help it reach customers seeking pre-integrated security tools. highlights.content: DataCenterNews US - Specialist news for cloud & data center decision-makers [![DataCenterNews US logo](/brands/dcn-new-logo.svg) United States](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.com) ![Trane launches LiquidStack CDU 2.X for AI data centres](https://datacenter.news/uploads/story/2026/10/13/scott-smith-story-321214.webp) [DC](https://datacenter.news/tag/data-centers) [AI Infrastructure](https://datacenter.news/tag/ai-infrastructure) [NVIDIA](https://datacenter.news/tag/nvidia) # Trane launches LiquidStack CDU 2.X for AI data centres Mon, 12th Oct 2026 (Today) [![Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://datacenter.news/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor](/author/joseph-gabriel-lagonsin) Trane Technologies has launched the LiquidStack CDU 2.X coolant distribution unit for AI data centres, designed to support current and emerging GPU platforms. The product targets operators making cooling infrastructure decisions before finalising the computing hardware they will deploy, as rack densities rise and processor roadmaps continue to shift. **Liquid cooling demand** Liquid cooling is becoming a greater focus for the data centre industry as AI workloads push heat loads in server racks beyond the range typically handled by conventional air cooling. In this context, coolant distribution units have become central to liquid-cooled system design because they manage the flow of coolant between facility water systems and IT equipment. Trane says the CDU 2.X uses a common design intended to work across different AI silicon platforms, including current systems and forthcoming products such as NVIDIA Vera Rubin. The unit has flow capability of up to 3,750 litres per minute at 3.5 bar. According to Trane, the new unit can be configured for end-of-row and rack-adjacent deployment. It also offers options for control valves, power feeds and redundancy arrangements, allowing operators to align installations with different facility layouts and resilience requirements. **Flexible deployment** A key design goal is to limit the need for redesign when hardware plans change. That issue has become more pressing for data centre operators and developers that must commit to power and cooling infrastructure well before the final rack architecture is known. Trane also says the CDU 2.X uses an ultra-low-harmonics variable frequency drive architecture designed to address harmonic distortion at the source. This can reduce the need for additional power-quality components and simplify system design. Other specifications include support for facility inlet temperatures of up to 45C and lower approach temperatures, which Trane says can support efficient liquid cooling system layouts. **Expanded portfolio** The launch expands Trane's broader liquid cooling portfolio under the LiquidStack brand. The company recently made its GigaModular CDU platform commercially available with an expanded capacity of 14 MW, broadening its offer for operators building high-density AI infrastructure. Scott Smith, General Manager of LiquidStack at Trane Technologies, said the new system is intended to address the pace of change in AI infrastructure planning. "Operators need cooling infrastructure that can adapt as GPU platforms and rack densities evolve," said Scott Smith, General Manager of LiquidStack at Trane Technologies. "CDU 2.X combines the performance and flexibility customers need today with the headroom to prepare for what comes next, allowing them to configure cooling around their facility and deployment strategy rather than designing the facility around the CDU," added Smith. highlights.content: [AI/ML](/topic/aiml), [AI benefits/risks](/topic/ai-benefitsrisks), [Hardware](/topic/hardware) # Microsoft puts AI agents in security containers on Windows 11 ![Microsoft Logo on a Modern Glass Office Building](/api/thumbor-proxy?width=1920&src=https%3A%2F%2Ffiles.cyberriskalliance.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F02%2F021125_microsoft.jpg) (Adobe Stock) Microsoft has announced significant advancements in its AI strategy, focusing on enhancing the security of Windows devices for AI agents and introducing new capabilities for its Copilot AI assistant. As detailed by CRN, the company is making its Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) available for general use, aiming to provide robust security for AI workloads. Microsoft's new strategy includes making execution containers generally available to secure AI agents on Windows 11, with Intune policies to manage them. The company is also rolling out "hybrid intelligence" for Copilot, powered by GitHub's HydraFusion, allowing the AI to leverage local PC data and models for enhanced performance. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang emphasized the importance of MXC for the future of AI agent development. New Copilot+ PCs, featuring Nvidia's RTX Spark, are now available for pre-order, promising powerful local AI processing. Partner devices from Dell, HP, Lenovo, Asus, and MSI will also incorporate these AI capabilities. Additionally, upcoming DGX Station systems will bring advanced AI workloads and frontier models directly to Windows devices, enhancing local inferencing and data security for businesses and researchers. Logo, Blocks&Files](/view-resources/dachser2/public/blocksandfiles/logo-white.svg)](https://www.blocksandfiles.com) BANDF AD # Uvi gives AI agents enterprise context Chris Mellor [Chris Mellor](https://www.blocksandfiles.com/author/chris-mellor) STORAGE EDITOR Blocks & Files editor Published Israeli startup [Uvi](https://www.uvi.io/) says enterprises enterprises are paying frontier AI companies to repeatedly re-learn what their own businesses already know but cannot surface. It can reveal this hidden context using knowledge graph technology. Uvi says every AI agent an enterprise deploys starts work knowing nothing about the company it works for. It has to reconstruct that context from scratch, and the company pays a frontier model every time it does. It has knowledge graph technology to give Claude, Gemini, GPT and every other AI tool a company uses the missing context behind its decisions, conversations and code, creating a context reasoning layer the company owns once and can make available to every agent it runs. ![Gilad Salinger.](https://image.blocksandfiles.com/5302518.webp?imageId=5302518&x=0.00&y=0.00&cropw=100.00&croph=100.00&width=960&height=960&format=jpg) Gilad Salinger CEO and co-founder Gilad Salinger said: "Enterprise context is a problem that gets bigger as AI adoption grows. And speed depends on context: understanding what the organization knows, what other agents are changing in parallel, and the history behind those decisions, then narrowing it down to exactly what each agent needs to keep moving." The launch gives security teams a new way to create deception playbooks by describing a security objective in natural language. The agent then generates a strategy, deployment plan and playbook for use through Acalvio's ShadowPlex platform. Deception tools are used to mislead attackers, detect reconnaissance and expose unauthorised movement through systems. Acalvio is introducing the agent as companies face a rise in AI-assisted attacks, including faster reconnaissance, credential abuse and lateral movement across networks. The agent is intended to reduce the specialist knowledge usually needed to build and deploy deception programmes. Tasks that often required experienced deception engineers can now be completed in minutes through an AI-driven workflow. **How it works** Security teams can enter objectives such as detecting lateral movement, identifying credential abuse, protecting privileged identities or securing enterprise AI agents and AI-enabled infrastructure. The agent then reasons through the requirement and returns a structured deception playbook ready for deployment. The system is designed for both conventional enterprise environments and newer AI-focused deployments. Playbooks can be created for on-premises infrastructure, cloud environments, identity systems, IT and OT networks, and enterprise AI infrastructure. That broad scope reflects two security pressures facing many large organisations. One is attackers' use of AI to automate and accelerate intrusion activity. The other is the rapid adoption of AI agents and AI-enabled workflows inside companies, creating a new set of systems and identities that also need protection. **AI Focus** The ShadowPlex AI Agent is designed to address both sides of that trend. In one use case, security teams can generate playbooks to disrupt AI-driven reconnaissance, credential abuse and lateral movement. In another, they can use the same approach to protect internal AI agents, workflows and infrastructure from misuse, compromise and unauthorised access. For cybersecurity vendors, the ability to tie products to large AI ecosystems has become increasingly important as customers look for tools that fit into existing cloud and AI software estates. Placement in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Marketplace gives Acalvio visibility within Google Cloud's enterprise AI environment and could help it reach customers seeking pre-integrated security tools. AI Agents.content: [AI/ML](/topic/aiml), [AI benefits/risks](/topic/ai-benefitsrisks), [Hardware](/topic/hardware) # Microsoft puts AI agents in security containers on Windows 11 ![Microsoft Logo on a Modern Glass Office Building](/api/thumbor-proxy?width=1920&src=https%3A%2F%2Ffiles.cyberriskalliance.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2025%2F02%2F021125_microsoft.jpg) (Adobe Stock) Microsoft has announced significant advancements in its AI strategy, focusing on enhancing the security of Windows devices for AI agents and introducing new capabilities for its Copilot AI assistant. As detailed by CRN, the company is making its Microsoft Execution Containers (MXC) available for general use, aiming to provide robust security for AI workloads. Microsoft's new strategy includes making execution containers generally available to secure AI agents on Windows 11, with Intune policies to manage them. The company is also rolling out "hybrid intelligence" for Copilot, powered by GitHub's HydraFusion, allowing the AI to leverage local PC data and models for enhanced performance. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang emphasized the importance of MXC for the future of AI agent development. New Copilot+ PCs, featuring Nvidia's RTX Spark, are now available for pre-order, promising powerful local AI processing. Partner devices from Dell, HP, Lenovo, Asus, and MSI will also incorporate these AI capabilities. Additionally, upcoming DGX Station systems will bring advanced AI workloads and frontier models directly to Windows devices, enhancing local inferencing and data security for businesses and researchers. AI Agents.content: [Journal**Arta**](/en/) [ID](https://journalarta.com/)[EN · GLOBAL](/en/) Monday, October 12, 2026 · JakartaS&P 7,800.47 ▼0.14%USD/IDR 17,894 ▲0.49%Subscribe [Journal**Arta**](/en/) Global Edition beyond headlines Advertisement [**Markets**](/en/category/markets/) Markets · Stocks # Nvidia’s AI Agent Breakthrough Adds Fuel to Bullish Stock Forecasts ?s shares carry a striking market wager: some Wall Street price targets reach $743, more than three times the $205 share price cited in recent By **Alistair Sterling** October 12, 20262 min read ![Nvidia’s AI Agent Breakthrough Adds Fuel to Bullish Stock Forecasts](/en/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fjournalarta.com%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2026%2F10%2Fbank-4508-1-ai-ja-hero-1200x675.jpg&w=3840&q=75) Nvidia’s AI Agent Breakthrough Adds Fuel to Bullish Stock Forecasts Nvidia’s shares carry a striking market wager: some Wall Street price targets reach $743, more than three times the $205 share price cited in recent coverage. A new research result offers another reason for investor optimism, though it does not settle whether the stock can reach that level. The company’s Agentic Variation Operators (AVO) system scored 100% on the public set of ARC-AGI-3, an interactive reasoning benchmark, completing all 183 levels across 25 environments. The result underscores a broader shift in AI development: performance on extended tasks can depend on how an agent uses memory, tools and feedback, not just on the underlying model. ## Agent system pushes model score higher Nvidia said its research project lifted Claude Opus 5 from a 30% model baseline to a perfect score when deployed as part of the full AVO system. The agent completed the benchmark using about 12% fewer environment actions than VISTA, which used the same underlying model. AVO combines persistent memory with supervisory intervention to keep autonomous systems working through long tasks. In a separate test, the system ran for seven days on DGX B200 computers to optimize attention kernels. It explored more than 500 approaches and produced kernels that outperformed cuDNN by up to 3.5% and FlashAttention-4 by up to 10.5%. Advertisement The results are relevant to Nvidia’s business as AI workloads expand beyond training toward inference and agentic applications. Its next-generation Vera Rubin platform, described in source material as being in full production, is designed for those workloads and is expected to begin shipping in the coming months. ## Ambitious targets meet a historic valuation Recent coverage put Nvidia’s market capitalization at about $5 trillion, with shares around $205 after stock splits. LLMs.content: **[Help Net Security newsletters](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/newsletter/)**: Daily and weekly news, cybersecurity jobs, open source projects, breaking news – **[subscribe here!](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/newsletter/)** Please turn on your JavaScript for this page to function normally. ![Anamarija Pogorelec](https://img.helpnetsecurity.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/16092207/anamarija_pogorelec-100x100.jpg) [Anamarija Pogorelec](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/author/anamarijapogorelec/ "Author archive: https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/author/anamarijapogorelec/"), Senior Staff Writer, Help Net Security **Share** # Microsoft’s new model helps AI agents judge their next move Microsoft-Decision-1 is a small decision-scoring model. Given a situation, a question and a fixed set of [answer options](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/03/sans-aws-agentic-ai-security/), it returns a calibrated probability for each option. “This model is designed for routing, classification, prioritization, verification, and workflow control, making it easier to incorporate decision intelligence into existing applications, agents, and workflows in a secure, trusted environment,” [Achint Srivastava](https://www.linkedin.com/in/achint/), VP of Software Engineering in Microsoft’s Office of the CTO, [explained](https://commandline.microsoft.com/microsoft-decision-1-model-foundry/). ### How Microsoft-Decision-1 works Microsoft said it evaluated the model across 36 benchmarks covering nearly 150,000 questions, with the benchmarks kept blind from training. In the company’s benchmarking, Microsoft-Decision-1 was 2.5 times faster than H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1, the runner-up on speed, and about 35 times faster than [GPT-6 Sol](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/23/gpt-6-sol-luna-lower-api-prices/) in median latency. Accuracy, latency and calibration, side by side (Source: Microsoft) The probability scores indicate the model’s confidence in each answer and can help an application decide whether to act, defer a decision or request a review. Microsoft advises developers to validate the model and confidence thresholds on examples representative of their intended use. Microsoft-Decision-1 was post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B for single-pass scoring. The company plans to base future versions on other models, including those from [Microsoft AI](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/15/microsoft-ai-safety-rules-humanist-ai-code-of-conduct/) and OpenAI. The model supports yes/no questions, multiple-choice questions, rating scales and rubric-based grading of AI responses and agent actions through structured API calls. It is not designed for open-ended text generation, conversation, translation or summarization. The company identified speed, performance across tasks, robustness, probability calibration and safety as challenges in developing the model. ### Internal testing Microsoft is testing Microsoft-Decision-1 on tasks including sorting customer feedback, evaluating AI answers and finding relevant information during service incidents. Xbox researchers used it to group more than 10,000 pieces of feedback and reviews from surveys, STEAM and X into predefined categories. Microsoft said the results were competitive in quality with GPT-6 Sol’s, with processing more than 14 times faster at one two-hundredth of the cost. The Copilot team tested the model’s ability to assess chat and agent responses. Microsoft reported results competitive with [GPT5.6 Luna’s](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/06/29/openai-gpt-5-6-models-preview/), with processing 100 times faster. In incident-response tests, Microsoft-Decision-1 performed better and faster at retrieving relevant information than the large language model used for comparison. Microsoft also tested the model in Microsoft Discovery, where [AI agents](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/25/ariel-assaraf-coralogix-ai-agent-guardrails/) evaluate experiment results and revise their next steps. The Full variant ties Claude Sonnet 5.5 for the top tier globally, edging out OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra. On the long-horizon coding benchmark SWE-Marathon, both new models surpass Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. Trained at the gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center, the models support 1 million-token context windows and native multimodal input, with core capabilities including Active Memory and Active Focus. LLMs.content: ![Notebookcheck Logo](fileadmin/templates/nbc_v5/images/logo_alone_header.svg) ![Notebookcheck Logo](fileadmin/templates/nbc_v5/images/logo_simplified_unicolor_t.svg) ![dark mode](/fileadmin/templates/images/moon-filled.svg) ![light mode](/fileadmin/templates/images/sun-filled.svg) ![EN Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/us.svg) ![DE Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/de.svg) ![US Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/us.svg) ![ES Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/es.svg) ![FR Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/fr.svg) ![IT Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/it.svg) ![NL Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/nl.svg) ![PL Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/pl.svg) ![PT Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/pt.svg) ![RU Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/ru.svg) ![TR Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/tr.svg) ![SE Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/se.svg) ![CN Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/cn.svg) ![HU Flag](/fileadmin/templates/images/svg_flags/hu.svg) # Intel's new GPU packs up to 480GB of memory — but skips 3D graphics ![Intel GPU D270 — an AI accelerator designed for inference workloads.](fileadmin/_processed_/e/3/csm_intel_gpu_D270_ai_01_e8e2e50240.jpg) Intel has revealed the first accelerator in its GPU D-series, previously known by the codename Crescent Island: the D270, a data-center card built for AI inference rather than conventional 3D graphics. Based on Intel’s Xe3P architecture, the accelerator can be configured with up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory. One of the accelerator’s most unusual features is its memory configuration. Intel’s own reference card comes with 160GB of LPDDR5X, while its manufacturing partners can develop versions with up to 480GB. Rather than using high-bandwidth memory (HBM), as many competing AI accelerators do, the D270 relies on LPDDR5X. Intel is prioritizing memory capacity and deployment costs for inference workloads, where large language models need substantial amounts of memory to store model weights and manage long conversations. The accelerator offers 1.5TB/s of memory bandwidth and a peak FP8 performance of 1.3 petaflops. It has a 350W power target and uses an air-cooled PCIe 5.0 x16 design, allowing it to fit into conventional server infrastructure without requiring specialized liquid-cooling systems. The GPU contains 32 Xe3P cores, 256 XMX engines for accelerated matrix operations and 32MB of unified L2 cache. Intel has removed conventional 3D-graphics and ray-tracing hardware, allowing more silicon area to be dedicated to compute and AI processing. Consequently, the D270 is not a gaming graphics card, despite being based on GPU technology. Intel says the GPU D-series is intended for large language models, long-context inference and services that handle multiple AI requests concurrently. A single card can accommodate models with up to roughly 300 billion parameters, while a server equipped with eight accelerators can support models exceeding one trillion parameters. Intel lists potential uses including agentic AI, enterprise assistants, coding assistants, document understanding, multimodal AI, diffusion models and high-concurrency serving. Intel says customer sampling is underway with server manufacturers, cloud providers and software vendors. The company has not announced pricing or a general availability date for the GPU D-series. ![The Intel GPU D270 is based on a relatively compact GPU that lacks dedicated 3D-graphics and ray-tracing hardware](fileadmin/_processed_/7/3/csm_intel_gpu_D270_ai_02_cda3ed4082.jpg) ## Source(s) [Intel](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/newsroom/news/artificial-intelligence/intel-accelerates-open-infrastructure-agentic-ai-era.html) ![Google Logo](/fileadmin/templates/images/sociallinks/google_logo.svg) ![Facebook Logo](/fileadmin/templates/images/sociallinks/facebook_logo.svg) ![Threads Logo](/fileadmin/templates/images/sociallinks/threa...

The company reported blockbuster results in fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 along with strong guidance. MU is set to continue its excellent performance through 2027 and beyond on extremely tight supply of DRAM, soaring demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), soaring growth of physical layer artificial intelligence (AI), new Strategic Customer Agreements (SCAs) to reduce earnings and cash flow volatility and effective strategic investment. The chart below shows the price performance of MU year to date. **Robust Business Opportunity** AI is becoming a major structural growth driver for Micron. Advanced AI systems need much more memory capacity and bandwidth, supporting demand for HBM, advanced DRAM and high-performance data center SSDs. In contrast to traditional computing, AI computing desperately needs high-end memory chips without which, the Agentic AI and Large Language Models (LLMs) are impossible to run. Micron has been benefiting tremendously from the enormous growth of physical AI in day-to-day life, which has pushed up the demand for its memory chips. Tight DRAM supply remains a major earnings driver for MU. Fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 DRAM revenue reached $39.8 billion, or about 73% of total sales, rising 27% sequentially. Bit shipments increased in the mid-single-digit range, while prices increased in the high-teens percentage range. These gains helped lift MU’s non-GAAP gross margin to 87.0% from 84.9% in the prior quarter and 45.7% a year earlier. The situation for the DRAM crunch is likely to continue at least till 2028. AI workloads are driving higher memory requirements as models become larger and more complex. Growing model sizes, longer context windows and higher usage are increasing the amount of DRAM and storage needed to run AI efficiently. **Long-Term SCA Deals** As of fourth-quarter fiscal 2026, MU had signed 26 take-or-pay SCAs, which management estimates will represent more than 35% of revenues through 2030. Three-quarters of that expected revenue has a defined pricing framework, with most of those agreements using floor-and-ceiling bands. The contracts now extend into 2031, including two one-year extensions. Customer financial commitments tied to the signed SCAs and extensions have risen to $32 billion, mostly cash deposits. Remaining performance obligations are approximately $150 billion for agreements with determined pricing frameworks, based on committed volumes and minimum pricing. These new SCAs could provide more predictable demand and pricing while helping the company manage future memory cycles. Its rivals, such as **SK Hynix Inc.** SKHY and **Sandisk Corp.** SNDK are pursuing strategies similar to MU by building stronger customer commitments. **Strong Guidance** For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Micron expects revenues of $61.5 billion, plus or minus $1.5 billion. Non-GAAP gross margin is projected at approximately 86.25%, operating expenses at about $2.06 billion and earnings at $38.15 per share, plus or minus $1. Attorneys can now use AI-powered platforms to summarize deposition transcripts, organize discovery, draft contracts and generate preliminary research in a fraction of the time previously required. Technology vendors promise enormous gains in efficiency and client service. Against this backdrop, AI’s capabilities resurrect a familiar question with newly urgent stakes: When lawyers or clients share information with an AI platform, how do we ensure traditional protections such as the [attorney-client privilege](https://valawyersweekly.com/tag/attorney-client-privilege/?taxo-tag-body "Posts tagged with Attorney-client privilege") or the [work product doctrine](https://valawyersweekly.com/tag/work-product-doctrine/?taxo-tag-body "Posts tagged with work product doctrine") continue to apply? For centuries, privilege has rested on a simple premise: Clients must be able to communicate candidly with their lawyers without fear that those communications will later be disclosed. The doctrine has survived revolutions in communication — from handwritten correspondence to email — because its focus has never been the technology through which communications occur. Rather, privilege depends upon a confidential attorney-client relationship and communications made for the purpose of obtaining legal advice. Generative AI presents the next major test of that principle. Two 2026 court rulings offer signposts for how these questions will be analyzed, and how firms and companies should leverage AI tools while protecting privilege. **Privilege protects relationships, not conversations about the law** The privilege protects confidential communications between attorney and client, ensuring the uninhibited candor required to give and receive sound legal advice. The work product doctrine likewise shields materials prepared by or for counsel in anticipation of litigation, so that counsel can work without fear of disclosing legal theories and strategy. AI Product.content: Nearly two decades ago, a young college student wrote his final thesis about software capable of generating design documents for school buildings. Al Drams was studying architecture — following in the footsteps of his parents and grandfather — but it was technology that really intrigued him. There was just one problem: the technology his idea required didn’t exist yet. “Then ChatGPT came along,” said Drams, recalling when OpenAI released the generative AI chatbot that uses large language models (LLMs) in November 2022. His old idea suddenly seemed a lot more possible. Within six months, he launched the concept of Blueprints AI, a startup that uses AI to produce code-compliant and permit-ready architectural construction blueprints in minutes from a 2D sketch or PDF. Blueprints AI, which Drams officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200, a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt, taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco. During that 20-year lead-up to Blueprints AI, Drams earned his bachelor’s and master’s degrees in architecture from the University of Tehran and completed two years of Ph.D. coursework on digital design at the European Graduate School in Switzerland. He moved to the United States and opened an architecture firm in 2018 called Drams Architects. Then, after obtaining a general contractor’s license, he added a construction business in 2021. Drams should have been satisfied. He wasn’t. “I was saying, okay, maybe I can build new projects that change people’s life in that area, but it wouldn’t be a big impact,” he said. “What makes me very excited about technology is the impact, the hours saved, the energy saved of people doing the same thing over and over and over.” Blueprints AI will unveil a more capable second-generation version of its software at Disrupt. Drams and Cao say it will make a big impact because it takes over the repetitive drafting work that fills most of an architect’s day. “It will make better spaces for people because now architects have the time to design,” said Drams. He said architects spend about 80% of their time on drafting and only 20% on design. “I want to flip that to be 20-80.” Drams and Cao met at an AI conference several years ago and combined their skills to build the company. Cao, a data scientist from Hong Kong, handles sales and go-to-market strategy as chief commercial officer. The pair trained their models using eight years of approved drawing sets from Drams’ design and construction firm, which is still in business. Its first-generation software produces architectural construction documents and costs between $3,200 to $8,500 a month, depending on the plan. Custom pricing for enterprises is also available. The startup’s second-generation software will deliver a considerable upgrade. Customers can start with a description or sketch of a project and create blueprints for every aspect of a building at once, including architecture, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and interior design. Version 2 allows users to design and make changes to the project, an upgrade over the first iteration. Importantly, one design change updates the entire project and is checked against local building codes. Early customers are already using the second version, and Drams said it will become publicly available this week. The startup is already working on a third version of its software that will add in structural analysis and electrical panel design. The technology doesn’t replace licensed architects, according to the co-founders. Licensed professionals still review the documents and affix their seal before submitting them for permits. The unit will embed Claude and Claude Code into HCLSoftware products and the AI Force platform, signaling a major push into generative‑AI SaaS for enterprise customers. ## Why It Matters The HCLTech‑Anthropic partnership illustrates how traditional enterprise services firms are re‑architecting their go‑to‑market strategies around AI‑native SaaS. By embedding Claude directly into its software suite, HCLTech can monetize AI through recurring subscription fees, cross‑sell to its existing customer base, and differentiate on governance—a critical concern for regulated industries. The move also raises the bar for competitors, forcing them to consider deeper model integration rather than offering generic cloud APIs. For operators, the announcement underscores the growing importance of building dedicated AI business units and centers of excellence that can deliver secure, sandboxed environments. Companies that can combine agentic AI with robust governance will likely capture higher net‑retention and expansion revenue, while those that rely on bolt‑on AI risk lower margins and higher churn. ## Key Points 1. HCLTech announced a Global Premier Partnership with Anthropic on Oct. 12, 2026. 2. A dedicated Anthropic Business Unit and Center of Excellence will be created. 3. Claude and Claude Code will be embedded into HCLSoftware products like BigFix and AppScan. 4. AI Force platform will integrate Anthropic models, supporting on‑prem, hybrid and cloud deployments. 5. Partnership focuses on safety, cybersecurity, and governance for enterprise AI. ## Analysis HCLTech’s strategy reflects a broader industry trend where legacy IT services firms are transitioning to AI‑centric SaaS models. Historically, such firms have relied on project‑based revenue, which is vulnerable to economic cycles. By locking Anthropic’s models into its product stack, HCLTech can shift to a subscription‑driven model with higher predictability and margin potential. The emphasis on agentic AI—where autonomous agents perform complex tasks—aligns with the next wave of enterprise automation, moving beyond simple text generation to workflow orchestration. From a competitive standpoint, the partnership gives HCLTech a differentiated offering that blends Anthropic’s safety‑first model philosophy with HCL’s deep domain expertise in cybersecurity and IT operations. Rivals like Microsoft and Google provide powerful LLMs but often lack the vertical integration that HCLTech can deliver. This could translate into higher net‑retention rates as customers adopt AI modules that are tightly coupled with their existing tools and compliance frameworks. Looking ahead, the success of the Anthropic Business Unit will hinge on execution. HCLTech must demonstrate that its sandboxed deployments can meet stringent enterprise governance standards while delivering measurable productivity gains. If it can do so, the unit could become a template for other services firms seeking to monetize AI through SaaS, potentially reshaping the revenue mix of the broader enterprise software market. ## 10Sources [![](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=www.unite.ai&sz=64)HCLTech Forms Anthropic Business Unit Under Global Premier Partnershipunite.ai](https://www.unite.ai/hcltech-forms-anthropic-business-unit-under-global-premier-partnership/)...

Its engineers work inside a client’s own systems and across departments, from sales and marketing to customer success, finance, and operations. Platforms don’t do that on their own.” The launch comes as enterprises race to adopt AI while struggling to move beyond pilots. Gartner predicts that more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be cancelled by the end of 2027, citing escalating costs, unclear business value and inadequate risk controls. The gap between AI investment and execution is creating demand for engineers who can turn technology into working business systems. Investors are now forming advisory programmes around forward-deployed engineering. Gartner found that 58% of customers who use generative AI have used it to complete a task on their behalf, rising to 74% in B2B settings. Customers increasingly expect AI to book, submit, order, and escalate, not just reply. That raises the stakes for how these systems are designed and governed. gartner Customers want convenience and a human option The same research shows customers are not rejecting AI. Gartner found that 50% say interactions are easier when companies use it, yet 87% still expect a route to a person. Gartner’s analyst notes that customers who are forced through several unsuccessful AI interactions before reaching a person are less likely to use the tool again. For enterprise leaders, the question is no longer how much can be automated, but where automation should stop and a human should take over. gartner A trust gap to close Trust is part of the equation. The Thales Digital Trust Index 2026 reports that only 23% of consumers trust companies to use AI responsibly with their data, and that 77% would not trust a company more simply because it uses generative AI [verify against the Thales source]. I'm also co-founder and chairman of Saigon A.I., a doctoral researcher at the University of St Andrews working between educational psychology and artificial intelligence with a focus on self-regulated learning (SRL), and the builder of QCoda, an AI governance platform focused on governing AI-assisted software engineering. QCoda started with a pattern I kept running into, in my own teams and in teams I advised. We'd make a dozen consequential decisions while planning an AI feature. Which model. Which data. Where it runs. Who gets to see the prompts. Nobody wrote any of it down. Months later an auditor (or a customer's security team, or a regulator) would ask why we did it that way, and the honest answer was that nobody really decided. It just happened. Governance showed up after the mistake, as punishment. That's the lens I bring here. Open Source AI.content: ### TCI Media: Home of the Wire Publications ![Header Logo 1](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/ai-600-300x73-1.webp) ![Header Logo 2](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/bigdatawire-logo.webp) ![Header Logo 3](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/qc-600-300x69-1.webp) ![Logo](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2025/11/hpc-logo-300x60-1.jpg) ## Off the Wire Press Releases ### October 12, 2026 ### October 9, 2026 ### October 8, 2026 ### October 7, 2026 ## H2O-Lightning-4B Ranks 1st on JevBench Open-Weights Leaderboard *A 4-billion-parameter open-source decision model finishes ahead of 103 open-weight systems, including some built on base models nearly eight times its size, on a benchmark that weighs intelligence, calibration, speed and cost equally.* MOUNTAIN VIEW, Calif., Oct. 12, 2026 — [H2O.ai](https://h2o.ai/), the trusted Sovereign AI Platform for predictive, generative and agentic AI, with observability built in, today announced that **H2O-Lightning-4B**, its open-weights decision model, ranked first among 104 open-weight systems on the [JevBench Composite Score leaderboard](https://h2o.ai/blog/2026/h2o-lightning-jevbench/) as of Oct. 7. The model scores 72.5 out of 100, above the 71.5 posted by Jev, the benchmark’s closed API reference system, at an estimated $0.021 per 1,000 decisions. [![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px-300x300.jpg)](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px.jpg)Much of the AI work inside banks, insurers, health systems, telcos and government agencies is a decision about a record: route this ticket, flag this clause, score this claim. TypeSafe AI built Jev around that idea. Jev is a model that answers a typed question with a calibrated probability instead of generated text. Each decision needs the right answer, a probability a risk team can set a threshold on, a latency that fits a live workflow, and a cost that stays predictable at millions of calls a month. JevBench scores all four on an equal-weight harmonic mean, so a weak axis drags down the whole score. An open 4-billion-parameter model scoring above a closed reference system is the shift regulated buyers have been waiting for. Owning the model no longer means giving up quality. ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/aiwire/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2023/11/H2O-sunshine-Logo_1000px-300x300.jpg) “Better decisions don’t need bigger models. Classification is one of the most common enterprise use cases, and models like H2O-Lightning deliver frontier-model quality and lightning-fast decisions at about 100 times lower cost. Leading AI companies, including Microsoft, are now building decision models of their own. This is not a flash in the pan,” said Sri Ambati, Founder and CEO of H2O.ai. **How It Works** H2O-Lightning-4B is a fine-tune of Qwen3.5-4B. It answers typed decision questions about a record such as a document, ticket, policy or conversation, and returns a probability for every option. It supports three question types: choice (one of a set of named options), yes/no (the probability that a statement is true) and score (an ordinal level on a stated scale, with its probability distribution). Each decision is one forward pass and one output token, so cost is driven by input tokens alone. The model runs on unmodified vLLM 0.30.0 with a small standard-library shim in front. **The Results** H2O-Lightning-4B competes in a crowded, fast-moving field. TypeSafe AI set the bar with Jev. Independent developers and enterprise teams have since put more than 100 open-weight systems on the JevBench board, and its maintainers score every entry the same way. Open Source AI.content: There Are Free, Open-Source Versions of Microsoft Office Apps Thanks to AI [Subscribe](https://petapixel.com/members) [Sign In](https://petapixel.com/login/?redirect_to=https%3A%2F%2Fpetapixel.com%2F2026%2F10%2F12%2Fthere-are-free-open-source-versions-of-microsoft-office-apps-thanks-to-ai%2F) # There Are Free, Open-Source Versions of Microsoft Office Apps Thanks to AI [News](https://petapixel.com/topic/news/) [Jeremy Gray](https://petapixel.com/author/jeremygray/) * Copied! Brandon Thomas, the experienced software engineer behind the AI-assisted reverse engineering effort to [rebuild open-source versions of Adobe’s Creative Suite applications](https://petapixel.com/2026/10/07/someone-rebuilt-free-open-source-versions-of-photoshop-premiere-and-lightroom-using-ai/), including Photoshop, Premiere, and Lightroom, is setting his sights on another oft-maligned set of software: Microsoft Office. As Thomas’ ArtCraft Discord has grown considerably with the release and publicity surrounding his Adobe clones, the developer has been taking requests for which software to reverse engineer next using Anthropic’s Opus 5.5 AI LLM. Unsurprisingly, many people, like they are sick of paying for Adobe’s software, are tired of paying for Microsoft Office, including Microsoft Word and Excel. ![A Microsoft Word document titled ](https://petapixel.com/assets/uploads/2026/10/review_1-800x500.jpg) Microsoft Word gets rebuilt using AI. It’s now “WordCraft,” and open source. Thomas took the request and quickly started work on open-source Microsoft Office clones for macOS, Windows, and Linux. The Word clone, WordCraft, looks practically identical. The same goes for the Excel clone, GridCraft, and the PowerPoint look-alike, DeckCraft. Thomas is also working on an AutoCAD clone and a studio-grade audio mixer, SoundCraft. In response to criticism that he is churning out AI slop, [Thomas took to X](https://x.com/echelon) to tout his credentials. “My guy, I can code,” Thomas said in response to online criticism. “AI models enable me to work as an entire company. Open Source AI.content: [![techmonk logo](/_icons/logos/techmonk-logo-mobile-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [Cybersecurity](/news/cybersecurity) * 2 minRead # ARTEX AI, Claude agents used in South Korean bank cyberattacks A Chinese-speaking hacker used the ARTEX AI penetration testing suite and Claude agents in recent cyberattacks on South Korean financial institutions. These attacks exposed client data and caused system outages at banks including Shinhan Bank. * [TechGig](/agency/87450652/TechGig "TechGig") * Published On Oct 12, 2026 at 02:55 PM IST ## Highlights * Chinese hacker used ARTEX AI and Claude agents in South Korean bank cyberattacks. * Attacks targeted Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank, and Hana Bank, exposing client data. * ARTEX AI instance used DeepSeek v4.1-flash, GLM-5.3, and Grok 4.6 LLMs. * ARTEX developer closed the project after real-world attack confirmation. A Chinese-speaking hacker launched [cyberattacks](/tag/cyberattacks) on South Korean financial institutions earlier this month, using the [ARTEX AI](/tag/artex+ai) penetration testing suite and [Claude agents](/tag/claude+agents). Targets included [Shinhan Bank](/tag/shinhan+bank), KB Kookmin Bank, and Hana Bank, exposing clients' personal data and credit card information, and causing system outages in some cases. The South Korean government reacted with an emergency meeting and calls for immediate security measures for critical IT systems. Security firm [CrowdStrike](/tag/crowdstrike) confirmed the use of ARTEX [AI](/tag/ai), which was until recently an open-source agentic penetration testing suite developed in China. Researchers identified the attacker's infrastructure and found open directories with Claude Code session histories, ARTEX configuration files, and Claude memory files. The ARTEX instance used [DeepSeek v4.1-flash](/tag/deepseek+v4.1-flash) as the primary large language model (LLM) backend, and the threat actor supplemented this LLM with [GLM-5.3](/tag/glm-5.3) (Zhipu AI) and [Grok 4.6](/tag/grok+4.6) for additional Claude Code sessions, CrowdStrike explained. The threat actor likely accessed DeepSeek via the LLM API proxy/reseller xcai[.]pro, researchers noted. Once an agent is inside a project, it also picks dependencies, reads documentation, and writes code against your API, often without a human opening your README at all. So a new question for OSS maintainers is how to make a project legible to agents. I'll use a small, real project as the case study: `markdown-regex`, a zero-dependency TypeScript library of ready-made RegExp constants for parsing Markdown. It has a solid base: a clear install section, an API table, TypeScript types, dual ESM/CommonJS builds, and CI across several Node versions. It also has about 11 stars, which makes it a good example of a useful project that most people, and most agents, will never encounter. ![Arthur's image-dad09](https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/3nhao37bBEfHA9RTQ0WNVWfXPD02-gq83b1a.jpeg?auto=format%2Ccompress&w=1920) Agents interact with your project in two ways, and each needs different work. In the first, they retrieve text (search results, registry pages, docs) to decide whether to recommend you. In the second, they read your repo and call your API to get a task done. The rest of this article covers both, plus the trust signals that influence each. ## Part 1: Be findable and recommendable ### State when to use it, and when not to An agent choosing a library needs a decision rule. Most READMEs describe what the project does but never say when it's the right choice. For a regex-based Markdown toolkit, that means saying plainly: use this for quick extraction, linting, and lightweight transforms; use a full parser like remark or markdown-it when you need a real AST, deeply nested structures, or strict CommonMark compliance. That honesty helps in two ways. Agents recommend you for jobs you're good at, and they stop recommending you for jobs you'd fail, which protects your reputation. ![Arthur's image-...

Infra & Chips.content: DataCenterNews US - Specialist news for cloud & data center decision-makers [![DataCenterNews US logo](/brands/dcn-new-logo.svg) United States](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.com) ![Trane launches LiquidStack CDU 2.X for AI data centres](https://datacenter.news/uploads/story/2026/10/13/scott-smith-story-321214.webp) [DC](https://datacenter.news/tag/data-centers) [AI Infrastructure](https://datacenter.news/tag/ai-infrastructure) [NVIDIA](https://datacenter.news/tag/nvidia) # Trane launches LiquidStack CDU 2.X for AI data centres Mon, 12th Oct 2026 (Today) [![Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://datacenter.news/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor](/author/joseph-gabriel-lagonsin) Trane Technologies has launched the LiquidStack CDU 2.X coolant distribution unit for AI data centres, designed to support current and emerging GPU platforms. The product targets operators making cooling infrastructure decisions before finalising the computing hardware they will deploy, as rack densities rise and processor roadmaps continue to shift. **Liquid cooling demand** Liquid cooling is becoming a greater focus for the data centre industry as AI workloads push heat loads in server racks beyond the range typically handled by conventional air cooling. In this context, coolant distribution units have become central to liquid-cooled system design because they manage the flow of coolant between facility water systems and IT equipment. Trane says the CDU 2.X uses a common design intended to work across different AI silicon platforms, including current systems and forthcoming products such as NVIDIA Vera Rubin. The unit has flow capability of up to 3,750 litres per minute at 3.5 bar. According to Trane, the new unit can be configured for end-of-row and rack-adjacent deployment. It also offers options for control valves, power feeds and redundancy arrangements, allowing operators to align installations with different facility layouts and resilience requirements. **Flexible deployment** A key design goal is to limit the need for redesign when hardware plans change. That issue has become more pressing for data centre operators and developers that must commit to power and cooling infrastructure well before the final rack architecture is known. Trane also says the CDU 2.X uses an ultra-low-harmonics variable frequency drive architecture designed to address harmonic distortion at the source. This can reduce the need for additional power-quality components and simplify system design. Other specifications include support for facility inlet temperatures of up to 45C and lower approach temperatures, which Trane says can support efficient liquid cooling system layouts. **Expanded portfolio** The launch expands Trane's broader liquid cooling portfolio under the LiquidStack brand. The company recently made its GigaModular CDU platform commercially available with an expanded capacity of 14 MW, broadening its offer for operators building high-density AI infrastructure. Scott Smith, General Manager of LiquidStack at Trane Technologies, said the new system is intended to address the pace of change in AI infrastructure planning. "Operators need cooling infrastructure that can adapt as GPU platforms and rack densities evolve," said Scott Smith, General Manager of LiquidStack at Trane Technologies. "CDU 2.X combines the performance and flexibility customers need today with the headroom to prepare for what comes next, allowing them to configure cooling around their facility and deployment strategy rather than designing the facility around the CDU," added Smith. Infra & Chips.content: ## Since 1987: Covering the Fastest Computers in the World and the People Who Run Them ### TCI Media: Home of the Wire Publications ![Header Logo 1](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/ai-600-300x73-1.webp) ![Header Logo 2](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/data-600-300x72-1.webp) ![Header Logo 3](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/qc-600-300x69-1.webp) ![Logo](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/hpc-logo-300x60-1.jpg) ## Off the Wire Press Releases ### October 12, 2026 ## NVIDIA and Cisco Introduce New Pluggable Optics Form Factor to Scale AI Factories *New Transceivers Enable AI Builders to Scale Compute Within the Same Network Footprint While Reducing Networking’s Share of the Power Budget* SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 12, 2026 — [NVIDIA](https://www.nvidia.com/) and [Cisco](https://www.cisco.com/) today announced plans for Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a new high-density 400Gb/s-per-lane optical module designed to equip the hardware ecosystem for the next generation of AI factories using pluggable transceivers. [![](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/nvidia-cisco-300x210.png)](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/nvidia-cisco.png)As AI models grow and inference demand expands, AI factories must connect more computing systems while managing network complexity, power and costs. Moving more data per watt and per switch helps operators make better use of their infrastructure investments. ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/nvidia-cisco-300x210.png) Scaling AI factories requires more bandwidth per connection and more connections per switch. When a switch reaches its capacity, further network expansion can require additional switch layers and optical links, increasing latency, power consumption and costs. USFP is designed to enable AI factory builders to scale from 200 Gb/s per lane to 400Gb/s-per-lane Ethernet AI fabrics, while extending a deployment model proven at scale across multiple generations of data center networks. With USFP, customers can embrace next-generation optical technology and meet the performance demand of AI workloads without overhauling their data center infrastructure. The first planned USFP-based transceivers will pack 16 full-duplex lanes in an octal small form factor (OSFP)-sized footprint supporting both switches and SuperNICs, with the ability to expand to 32 and more lanes in the future. By doubling both the lane count and bandwidth per lane, USFP enables AI fabrics to connect more 1.6Tb/s endpoints without adding network tiers. Customers will be able to achieve 12.8Tb/s of overall capacity with USFP. Comparable with an OSFP-sized module, it delivers 4x the bandwidth and front-panel bandwidth density, with approximately 1.3x the power efficiency, versus 200Gb/s-per-lane pluggable modules. This means AI builders can increase their compute scale within the same network footprint, while decreasing networking’s share of the overall AI factory power budget. “Building the world’s largest AI factories starts with rethinking the smallest of connections,” said Gilad Shainer, senior vice president NVIDIA. “With USFP, NVIDIA and Cisco are building an ecosystem to reinvent pluggable optics — connecting more computing with greater efficiency to power the next generation of AI factories.” “AI builders need an interconnect architecture that can scale performance without locking them into a more complex operating model,” said Bill Gartner, senior vice president and general manager of optical systems and optics at Cisco. “Cisco and NVIDIA recognized that scaling pluggable optics to 400Gb/s per lane would require more than another incremental extension of today’s module designs. Through our collaboration, USFP is designed to deliver a new level of bandwidth density while preserving the serviceability, deployment flexibility and operational simplicity of pluggable optics.
