Infra & Chips.content: IT Brief UK - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers [![IT Brief UK logo](/brands/itb-new-logo.svg) United Kingdom](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.co.uk) ![Texas Instruments launches chips to boost AI data centres](https://itbrief.co.uk/uploads/story/2026/10/13/TI_s_new_ADC34DSO75_is_the_first_analog-to-digital_converter_to_enable_247__low-power__event-based_remote_monitoring_at_nanosecond_resolution-story-321185.webp) [Semiconductors](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/semiconductors) [Hyperscale](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/hyperscale) [DC](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/data-centers) # Texas Instruments launches chips to boost AI data centres Mon, 12th Oct 2026 (Today) [![Sofiah Nichole Salivio](https://itbrief.co.uk/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNywicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--3f3cbcdb3f86206827b894ccc07566b24a1d49e6/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/unnamed%20(2).webp) SOFIAH NICHOLE SALIVIO News Editor](/author/sofiah-nichole-salivio) Texas Instruments has introduced three semiconductor products for AI data centres, focused on monitoring, power protection and timing in server and networking equipment. The new devices are the ADC34DSO75 analogue-to-digital converter, the LMI800PS isolated hot-swap controller and the LMK6B oscillator. They are intended to address power instability, fault detection and signal timing issues that can contribute to outages in AI infrastructure. The ADC34DSO75 is designed for continuous remote monitoring of power rails at nanosecond resolution. Existing monitoring systems can miss short-lived glitches that affect low-voltage, high-current rails in data centres. The chip samples at 3 gigasamples per second and uses on-chip digital signal processing to detect and capture transient fault events in real time. It is also intended to reduce the need for on-site debugging equipment such as oscilloscopes. Downtime has become a bigger issue as AI workloads expand and operators pack more computing equipment into each rack. Brief interruptions in power quality or system timing can affect clusters running training and inference tasks, where high utilisation and service availability come at significant cost. Data-centre outages can cost operators hundreds of thousands of dollars an hour. Earlier detection of brief power anomalies could help identify faults before they develop into larger interruptions. **Power architecture** The LMI800PS targets a separate shift in data-centre design as operators consider higher-voltage distribution systems to improve efficiency and manage the growing power demands of AI servers. The chip supports both ±400V and 800V distributions. Texas Instruments describes the LMI800PS as an 800V isolated hot-swap controller that combines functions that would otherwise require five integrated circuits. Its isolated bias supply and PMBus telemetry reduce board area by more than 60% compared with a discrete design. Hot-swap controllers allow equipment to be connected safely to live power systems while limiting in-rush current and protecting the power path. The device also supports fault isolation so that a failure in one load does not disrupt a shared power bus. The product includes 5kVrms reinforced isolation and more than 8mm creepage, which Texas Instruments says helps it meet relevant safety requirements for high-voltage systems. Those specifications matter as data-centre operators explore denser rack designs and more demanding power-delivery schemes. **Timing focus** The third product, the LMK6B, is a bulk acoustic wave-based oscillator designed for high-speed networking equipment. Infra & Chips.content: DataCenterNews US - Specialist news for cloud & data center decision-makers [![DataCenterNews US logo](/brands/dcn-new-logo.svg) United States](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.com) ![Gimlet & Cerebras to deliver AI inference at speed](https://datacenter.news/uploads/story/2026/10/13/zain-asgar-story-321205.webp) [LLMs](https://datacenter.news/tag/large-language-models) [AI](https://datacenter.news/tag/artificial-intelligence) [AI Infrastructure](https://datacenter.news/tag/ai-infrastructure) # Gimlet & Cerebras to deliver AI inference at speed Mon, 12th Oct 2026 (Today) [![Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://datacenter.news/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor](/author/joseph-gabriel-lagonsin) Gimlet and Cerebras have partnered to deliver AI inference through Gimlet Cloud, with a stated goal of speeds of up to 3,000 tokens per second. The agreement adds Cerebras as a supported accelerator within Gimlet's cloud service, which Gimlet describes as a multi-silicon inference platform. The company plans to deploy 100 MW of Cerebras-powered inference capacity, and the integrated system is already operating in private deployments. North America has played a central role in GPU development through its leadership in personal computing, gaming hardware, semiconductor design, and advanced visualization. The introduction of programmable shaders, parallel computing models, and general-purpose GPU computing expanded GPU deployment beyond graphics rendering. The technology is now integral to AI training, generative AI inference, high-performance computing, enterprise analytics, and data-intensive applications. Accelerated computing is reshaping demand across consumer and enterprise markets. Hyperscale cloud providers, AI developers, research institutions, automotive companies, healthcare analytics firms, and enterprises are investing in scalable GPU infrastructure. Key purchasing considerations include energy efficiency, advanced memory bandwidth, AI-optimized cores, thermal performance, refined chip architecture, and GPU-as-a-Service availability. Their dedicated processing capabilities, separate graphics memory, and workload acceleration support deep learning, advanced 3D rendering, simulation, and compute-intensive applications. Integrated GPUs continue to gain adoption across laptops, desktops, tablets, and mainstream devices due to compact system requirements, lower power consumption, cost efficiency, media processing, light gaming, and AI-enabled functionality.
